## 2026-11-15: cpp-threads, runtime/threads.cpp's crash diagnosed: bin/cppi built C++ programs with the seed's ci (branch `cpp-threads` from `mac/revisit-1115` `3d0cae3c1`)

- The brief (B1, tonight's gate): runtime/threads.cpp, recorded in `:thread-exceptions` as a segmentation fault in `_ZL4worki`,
  aborts through `std::terminate` from `std::this_thread::yield` since the C++ chain cpp-s13..cpp-s15 merged (ff30398d0); suspected
  cpp-s14's or cpp-s15's front end (CP395's noexcept, the conversion templates, the destroy landing pad).
- Not the front end: threads.cpp's IR by our route here and in next's `.tmp/cppi-check` (made at 1b381e60b, gate 13e's tree) are equal
  up to the inliner's counters, and their lowered C too. The abort's own message names the cause: thread 1003 (`work(2)`) terminates
  on `std::runtime_error("t0")`, thread 0's exception. The node program held the lowered runtime's `_Thread_local` `cx$pending` and
  `cx$cur` (arbace/cpp/rt/eh.c.ae, CP103 (b)) as plain statics, `(static 320 4 4 0 "cx$pending")`, on both trees: one pending flag for
  four threads. bin/cppi's `arbace_tool -m arbace.cpp.run` runs used stage 0's embedded ci (the seed d5548e72, 2026-11-05), older than
  ci's threads (de576f46b, 2026-11-06: `RO 2`, a block per thread); RT.toolSource does not reload `arbace/c/` from the checkout, which is
  why bin/ci, bin/llvmi and bin/rsi run under `bin/lib/ci/fresh.bash`'s `c_ci_fresh` (686246a33) and bin/cppi did not. A C probe of
  `_Thread_local` counters on four threads: `bad 79996` by the embedded ci, 0 by the checkout's. The old fault and the new abort are the
  same race: llvm-eh's `cx$exception` (writing the adjusted pointer into `cx$cur`) moved where it lands.
- Fix (crop paths only, no key moves): `bin/lib/cppi/ci-fresh.bash`'s `cppi_ci` runs every `arbace.cpp.run` step (read-lib, check-c,
  lower-lib, nodes-list, compile-list, nodes) under `c_ci_fresh` in a subshell; the front end, the lowering and the judges stay
  compiled. Alternatives: `c_ci_fresh` for the whole bin/cppi (every C++ front-end run evaluated too: slower for nothing); reloading
  `arbace.c.build` from inside arbace.cpp.run (a C namespace's loading decided by a C++ one, against fresh.bash's single rule); a
  re-seed (window W, not tonight). Cost: ci's prebuilt fragments are keyed by how its sources ran, so the first build at a key makes them
  with the evaluated builder (io.cpp's build 435 s once, threads.cpp's 138 s, then 56 s).
- Probe `test/cpp/selftest/tls.sh` (cpp-selftest; tls.cpp by our route): the statics `RO 2`, three runs pass; controls: the judge rejects
  `cx$pending` `RO 0`, and the build under `CI_FRESH=0` has it `RO 0`.
- Judged: `bin/cppi check --record` over samples and runtime (the gate's cpp-check parts): samples 7 of 7, runtime 7 pass and
  thread-throw.cpp in `:threads` as recorded, runtime/threads.cpp passes (9.8 s, g++'s digest): its row re-recorded `:pass` from `:fail`
  (`:thread-exceptions`, now without a member: CP396 proposed, (b) keep it until the weekly AOT runtime part confirms). The record run's
  nodes-list peaked 5.7 GB (3 threads, 6 GiB, the evaluated builder): CP397 proposed (cpp-check with the essential's `CPPI_THREADS=2
  CPPI_CI_MEMLIMIT=2GiB`). The watcher was raised from 2.5 to 6.5 GB for the record run (MemAvailable stayed above 37 GB): a rule slip, said.

## 2026-11-16: F26's slice, the class-file API compiled in the Go build (branch `f26-classfile`, from `b2-1115` 9e3d05d2b)

B2's joint world (java-night's slices, converted at 9e3d05d2b) did not compile: `go build ./jrt` gave 206 errors, 173 of them
F26's (172 in `ClassPrinterImpl`, 1 in `ClassReaderImpl`). The user decided B2 ships without F26 and F26 returns as its own
slice; this is that slice's work, on top of 9e3d05d2b (whose world still holds F26). Three root causes:

- **String is not a ConstantDesc.** With F26 the world translates ConstantDesc with its `resolveConstantDesc(Lookup)` (Lookup is
  translated since F15), so its Go interface has `ResolveConstantDesc_MethodHandles_Lookup__O`, which jrt's hand-written String
  lacked: ClassPrinterImpl passes string literals as ConstantDescs (172 errors) and j2g_up's `Up_String_ConstantDesc` failed.
- **Class is not a TypeDescriptor.OfField (nor a Constable).** F26 brings `java.lang.invoke.TypeDescriptor`; MethodType's
  bridges `parameterType`/`returnType` return Classes as OfFields (`Up_Class_TypeDescriptor_OfField`). jrt's Class had
  `descriptorString`, `isArray`, `isPrimitive`, `componentType` and `arrayType` but not the markers or the bridges.
- **A switch's lub.** `ClassReaderImpl.entryByIndex` assigns a switch of AbstractPoolEntry's subclasses (each a PoolEntry) to
  a PoolEntry. javac's type is the intersection AbstractPoolEntry & PoolEntry; the analyzer's `convert-node` converted each tail
  but kept the tails' unified type (the class part), so j2g declared an `AbstractPoolEntry_I` temporary and assigned it to the
  PoolEntry.

Fixes: a32a1401c (j2g's support code, `arbace/j2g/out.ae`, as for String.describeConstable: String's `resolveConstantDesc` and
its bridge; Class's `Is_TypeDescriptor`, `Is_TypeDescriptor_OfField`, the `componentType`/`arrayType` OfField bridges,
`Is_Constable` and `describeConstable` as `Optional.of(ClassDesc.ofDescriptor(descriptorString()))`, each written only when
its interfaces are in the world and jrt does not define it); 0ba1d5de3 (`arbace.classes.analyze/converted-type`: the switch,
if and if-instance cases of `convert-node` type the node `to` when the tails' unified type does not convert to it; and, because
the tools' host evaluates `arbace/classes` from its embedded copy (RT.toolSource names j2g's, not the front end's) until a
re-seed, j2g's `coerce` takes an abstract class or interface to an interface it is not a subtype of by jrt's `As`: in the
world's translation that changes one assignment, no other file's `As` count). Considered: jrt's manifest and hand-written
String/Class (jrt's own build has no Lookup, ClassDesc or TypeDescriptor types, so the methods cannot live in `go/arbace/jrt`;
the support code is where such members already are); a variant of ClassReaderImpl (the defect is the analyzer's, any such
switch would meet it).

After them, `go build -gcflags=-e ./jrt` at the gate build of 0ba1d5de3 (`bin/heavy-lock bin/arbace-go --gate-build` on the
next worktree's stage 0) reports **no F26 error**; 26 remain, all B2's non-F26 ones (ObjectInputStream's and SealedObject's
private accessors, GenericSignatureFormatError's and ConcurrentHashMap$Segment's super constructors, eleven `any(nil)` Lookups,
TypeAnnotationSupport/TypeAnnotationParser's Executable as an AnnotatedElement, HttpConnection's `Id__J`). None of them shares a
root cause with F26's. `bin/j2g-unit` on stage 0 passes; with the checkout's analyzer loaded over it (`J2G_UNIT_SOURCES`) its
six invokers tests fail the same with and without 0ba1d5de3 (the checkout's analyzer over the seed's world, not this change).

The run-time smoke `test/jrt/classfile/cfsmoke/ClassFileSmoke.java` (03739ada5; its expected output `ClassFileSmoke.out` from
jdk26u's JDK 26): builds a class (a branch, a loop, a field, stack maps by the default resolver), parses it element by element,
verifies and transforms it, and asks the String and Class contracts above. It is run by hand (its header), not a corpus test.

A fourth commit, 149432655: the interpreter reads a hand-written class's member table, so Class.describeConstable and
String.resolveConstantDesc also get table entries (j2g's support-table-forms, as String.describeConstable has); without
them the smoke stopped at "No accessible method describeConstable in java.lang.Class".

**The smoke ran.** B2's 26 non-F26 errors (and four more in package lang: `jrt.Member_Cast` undefined, MethodHandleInfo's
reflectAs in j2g_dyn; `any(nil)` Lookups in KeywordInvokeSite and ReflectorCallSite; `jrt.NN(any(nil))`) were stubbed by sed
in the gate build's generated module only (`.tmp/f26/scratch-hacks.sh` in the worktree, nothing committed), the executable
built from it (`.tmp/f26/scratch-build.sh`), and `test/java/run.ae --load files` ran the smoke's forms on it: **its output is
the JDK's byte for byte** (`ClassFileSmoke.out`). So once B2's own fixes land, F26 compiles and the API works on the runtime.

**Landing F26 on top of B2** (which removes it from the world): re-add `classfile-sources` to `test/jrt/jrt_sources.ae`'s world
(and the java.lang.constant/invoke/reflect parts B2 takes out with it), `bin/jrt-convert update` (35 GiB) and `bin/j2g-edge
update` (MethodHandleInfo's REF_ constants, Enum$EnumDesc, VarHandle$VarHandleDesc, as in F26's night commands), the forms'
and fixtures' updates, then this branch's four commits (cherry-picked: they are no-ops in a world without F26, each guarded by
`m/translated?`), a gate build, the smoke by its header's commands, and Java's levels on F26's 44 corpus tests.

## 2026-11-16: `bin/java-project`: a `META-INF` file in two modules shadowed, not an error (branch `ghidra-g1n`, from `mac/java-night` `989b6607a`)

- Found by the Ghidra demo's `bin/run-g1 analyze` (run by day while B2's build is fixed): SleighCompile's read stopped after
  every module read, merging `WORK/resources.all`, at `META-INF/DEPENDENCIES` in log4j-api and log4j-core (Maven's
  remote-resources output; their `LICENSE` and `NOTICE` too, equal by chance). Any program of two Apache artifacts hits it; so
  would night 18's `--build-program` of SleighCompile and of G1's tests.
- The rule: a `META-INF` file (not `META-INF/services`, still concatenated) in two modules that differ is the first module's in
  `resources.all`, as a class path's `getResource` answers in its order; the later ones are listed in `WORK/resources.shadowed`
  (path and module a line) and kept in their own `resources.jars/NNN-MODULE`, which is what `--build-program` gives j2g. A file
  outside `META-INF` in two modules that differ stays an error. Alternatives: dropping `DEPENDENCIES`, `LICENSE` and `NOTICE` as
  Maven metadata beside `META-INF/maven` (a program may read its notices; the class path keeps them), or the first copy of every
  duplicate (hides real conflicts of program data).
- Fixture: `test/java/project/controls/meta-dup.edn` (two source modules, each `META-INF/NOTICE`: the first kept, the second
  listed and in `002-b`) and the control `res-dup.edn` (`shared.txt` in both must fail, its message naming it). `bin/java-project
  test` 31 of 31 (main's stage 0, javac's tool `javac-f70d1a9d900eb07a9afc` with `REPR_JAVA_STALE_OK=1`). doc/go/BUILD.md's
  "Java sources by module".

  (`test/gate/plan.ae`'s `crop-tier?`, `crop-why`) runs such a step in the essential gate only when its crop's paths, its
  declaration or its environment changed since its latest pass, else decides `night` (deferred to the night's gate, explained in
  `bin/gate --plan`); a deferred step a running one needs is woken; `--rerun`, `GATE_CROP_DEFER=0`, the clean run and every night
  tier key them as before. The rules' files join the keys (GD3's `:also-changed` precedent), so the passes name them. The runner
  (`bin/lib/gate-run.bash`) and `bin/gate` take the status `night` (no run, no failure, no pass). `gate.crops check` requires a new
  crop's essential check in the tier and accepts a vector of controls.

  wasm-essential (5), llvm-essential (4), cpp-essential (3), si-essential (2), oi-essential (2), rust-read-essential (2): 20 steps

command for the crops (one more thing to remember by day). Result: after a re-seed the essential gate runs the core alone,

  `test/haskell/eval/run_plan.ae` builds a test whose all.T `only_ways` are all threaded ways `-threaded` (and takes T21651's
  Linux-conditional `extra_run_opts`); GHC 9.14.1's references of the 13 recorded such tests of the core recorded again by hand
  (`bin/hsi record-ref --only`, the oracle tier, light; T21969 with `HSI_REF_TIMEOUT=30`), their STG re-dumped into haskell-stg-progs;
  hsi's threaded way (`go/arbace/hs/threaded.ae`, new, and machine, nodes, compile, image, prim_ctl, rts, rtsapi, cprog, ffi, mem,
  the driver's -N): capabilities' count and setNumCapabilities, safe foreign calls to blocking host functions on goroutines of their
  own releasing the capability, bound threads and forkOS, a spark pool, hs_exit's exitScheduler; the I/O manager kept the
  non-threaded RTS's (rtsSupportsBoundThreads answered 0 to its modules). doc/haskell/HASKELL-EVAL-SURVEY.md, "As built: HES84 (a),
  the threaded way".
- **Why this design.** The machine's state is one goroutine's (thunks, stacks, ci's memory), so capabilities as goroutines are
  staged: stage 1 runs the Haskell threads on one evaluator and puts only what a program observes of the threaded RTS off it (a safe
  call that blocks); true parallel capabilities need the machine made concurrent (left). Considered: porting GHC's event manager
  (epoll, the timer manager: a large port for waits hsi already makes), and HES88's tried model of a safe sleep for every program
  (reverted then: the normal way's references differ; now it is the threaded way's alone).

## 2026-11-18: n-java-hoist, a postfix increment hoisted past a throw (repr/java, round 52, overnight)

Branch n-java-hoist from mac/n-java-conv 92eabf1b7. n-java-dates (mac/n-java-dates 667665e41, doc/classes/JAVA-DEFERRED-TRIAGE.md,
"As built: n-java-dates") found t05396's cause in the converter: `c = text.charAt(index++);` in SimpleDateFormat's
subParseNumericZone was converted `(set! c (.charAt text index)) (set! index ...)` (with-hoisting :after), so when charAt threw
the catch saw the old index (JLS 15.14.2: the variable is incremented when the increment is evaluated). Decision (a), taken
overnight (round 52), in its narrowest correct form: an increment whose variable is observable when the statement completes
abruptly, a field or a local a catch or finally of an enclosing try sees (one in scope at the try: lambdas cannot mutate a
captured local, and a local declared in the body is dead in the handlers, so neither loops nor lambdas need more), moves :after
only when nothing after it can throw (`x = i++` into a local or a field of `this`), else :before when nothing evaluated before it
can (literals, types, `this`, locals, fields of `this` by simple name, a call's target, an array element's array and index), else
it stays in place, `(let [old-N i] ...)`. Found on the way: plain :before (decision (a) as worded, and the return statements' and
fields' existing :before) is wrong too when something before the increment throws (`c = at(s.substring(5), i++)`), and fields
were exposed the same way (only through returns, an assignment statement disables the field path): both covered by the rule.
The printer folds `s; i++` back into `s` for such a local only for `x = i`. arbace/repr/java/convert.ae (hoistable-increments,
with-hoisting, hoist-mode, try-stmt's :guarded), print.ae (fold-increment, try-lines), CONVERTER-NOTES.md, PRINTER-NOTES.md.
Proof, light (each process under 1 GiB but two estimate batches at 1.04 and 1.07 GiB): a test file of 16 cases (i++, ++i, a[i++],
i--, finally, return, a throwing left operand, a local declared in the try, a lambda, fields, a qualified static call) read by
both fronts, equal; printed, read again, equal; javac on Arbace's class files equal to the original's; at interp on the gate's
e8e0d017243dca8a9f9f equal to the JDK's output (the old forms: 3 of 16 wrong). SimpleDateFormat's subParseNumericZone verbatim in
a driver: the old forms give the error indexes one short (t05396's "Bad error index=1, expected=2"), the new the JDK's. t05396
itself cannot run on tonight's executable with new forms: the runtime's classes cannot be redefined (go/arbace/jrt/dyn.ae's
DefineDynamic). jdk/forms: SimpleDateFormat's four statements; a sample, 0 of 155 java.base files and 1 of 59 likely ones

rustc-dev and rust-src apks taken from the pinned directory before `apk fetch` (which gives 1.100's); rustc-dev's absolute link

sysroot too; `pins check` checks the four apks and the tree's marker, and says "absent" in place of failing when no rustc is at the
pin. The proposal's name `REPR_RUST_RUSTC` became `ARBACE_RUSTC` with `ARBACE_RUSTC_HOME`: one variable for the gate's recipe and
the tools. Alternatives: LD_LIBRARY_PATH (would load LLVM 23.1.3 into the host's llvm tools), the tree on PATH set by the gate
alone (the tools by hand would still meet 1.100), a local apk repository and `apk add rust=1.99.1-r0` (RIND11 (d), installs).

## 2026-11-18: n-java-defer (round 54), review fixes: lt's uppercase from the first changing char; the keys' correction

Correction of the round-54 entry above (not edited): it says the shipped world's keys move for `arbace/j2g/model.ae`; they also move for
`arbace/classes/native.ae` and `go/arbace/jrt/locale.ae` (gate_key for all three, `arbace_runtime_key` and the javac keys for locale.ae
as a file of `go/arbace/jrt` / j2g's inputs as the triage's "Keys" paragraph says), not model.ae alone.

Fixed: `ltUpper` (go/arbace/jrt/locale.ae) dropped every U+0307 that follows a soft-dotted letter. The JDK (StringUTF16.toUpperCase,
openjdk/jdk26u `baf63fbe4`) copies the chars before `first`, the first char that is a surrogate or that changes case, as they are and
applies ConditionalSpecialCasing only from there. So `"ᵢ̇".toUpperCase(lt)` is `1D62 0307` (no char changes: the string is returned),
`"xᵢ̇"` `0058 1D62`, `"ᵢ̇̇"` `1D62 0307 0307`. ltUpper now finds `first` (isSurrogate, charToUpperEx) and drops only at i >= first.
Proof, as the round's: the file printed by `bin/repr-go print --layout gofmt`, in the stub module (`.tmp/keep/wt-n-java-defer-r54/lt-r2`, the
stubs' root upper made from the JDK's own table) against the JDK on jdk26u's java (26.0.2.1-internal): `j/Gen.java` writes the JDK's
`toUpperCase(lt)` of 4,448,265 strings (every non-surrogate code point c as c+U+0307, and with the prefixes i, U+1D62 and x) and nine
hand cases; `go test`: 4,448,265 of 4,448,265 equal (573 with a dot dropped), the 7 lt upperings of the tests, the 1,114,112 combining-class
buckets still equal; a control (the old rule, without `i >= first`) fails on `1D62 0307 0307` and 1,000s more. Nothing built.

## 2026-11-18: n-rust-aot, Rust's AOT cell 6 of 6: thread-locals in cf2g's library units (round 54)

The morning's entry left `test/rust/eval/threads.rs` in `:aot-thread-current` (status 134, std's `fatal runtime error: current thread
handle already set during thread spawn`). Same worktree and host: stage 0 `ARBACE_HOST_EXE=/root/arbace/target/seed/amd64/arbace`, the
worktree's own heavy lock.
- Cause: ci gives each thread its own block of thread-local objects (`go/arbace/ci/thread.ae`; static flag 2), and both the
  interpreter (`IStatic`) and cf2g's program code (`(g IDX)` of a static in the package's `:tls` set) reach it. A prebuilt library
  unit (RES34, `arbace.c.aotlib`) does not. In `translate-unit` a static is a placeholder `?sL`, and `"g"` compiled it to `G[S[L]]`,
  the main thread's static address, for every thread. std's `CURRENT` is in a std unit, so a spawned thread's `set_current` read the
  spawner's handle and rtaborted. The eval level runs the same units interpreted through `IStatic`, which is why it passes.
- Fix: a unit now has a table `T` (`Bind` fills it from the new `ci.Prog.TLSOffsets(s)`: the S entry's offset in a thread's block,
  -1 for the other statics) and a function `gs(t, l)`: the running thread's block plus the offset when it has one, else `G[S[l]]`.
  The `"g"` node of a static placeholder under `*reloc*` calls `gs`. The cost on a static that is not thread-local is one slice
  load and a compare.
- Finding: the aot-lib's Go key (`aotlib/lib-key*`) takes cf2g's bytes through `arbace.c.runtime/source-bytes`. That function counts
  only `arbace/repr/` as tool sources, but `RT.toolSource` also evaluates a changed `arbace/c/` from the checkout. So the key named
  the embedded cf2g and the stale units were reused: the first rerun linked the old std units, and I stopped it. Taken (round 54):
  bump `aotlib/aot-version` 1 to 2, since the units' Go format did change (T, gs, Bind). Not taken: making `source-bytes` follow
  `RT/toolSource`. `arbace/c/{check,build,run}.ae` already differ from stage 0's embedded copies, so that would move every runtime
  fragment key (std's and musl's fragments rebuilt) and belongs with the next re-seed's review.
- Proved: threads.rs alone (`--only`, the record's settings) passes. Then the whole samples corpus, `RSI_SHARD=1 RSI_THREADS=1
  RSI_JOBS=2 RSI_GO_P=1 RSI_CI_MEMLIMIT=1400MiB bin/heavy-lock bin/rsi check --aot --corpus samples --record`: 6 of 6 pass;
  compiled against interpreted, 5 both pass and 1 compiled only. That rewrote `test/rust/check-aot-linux-amd64.edn`, its times and
  `aot-inputs-linux-amd64.edn`, whose 6 rows came out unchanged. The new key's units were translated once into the main checkout's `.tmp/ci-aot-lib`
  (std's 55 MB, musl's, cb's and the ports'); the old key's directories are left to `bin/ci aot-lib prune`.
  C's `bin/ci check --aot --only test/c/essential-aot.txt` was also run on the new units: 10 of 10 pass compiled and interpreted, the controls differing as they must.
- Records: `:aot-thread-current` dropped from `test/rust/divergences-aot.edn` (now empty, with a comment). `test/crops/independence.edn`'s
  AOT :why says 6 of 6. `bin/rsi divergences --aot`. `bin/reap --record`: 54 of 56 cells checked, 0 problems; Rust AOT 6 / 0 / 0.
  `bin/crops-score --record` and `--judge --strict` (0 problems). `bin/records-check` (9 pairs, 0). Rust: completeness 95.8 to 99.99
  (meant 100), maturity 100, independence 80. go/arbace/ci is in gate_key, so the night's gate rebuilds the executables.
  Every process under 3 GiB; no gate.
- Alternatives not taken: keep the class and fix the compiled scheduler's swap at a thread start. The scheduler is not the cause,
  because the program's own code already reaches its thread-locals per thread. Copy the bytes at one address on each switch, as RE6's
  first design did: that breaks std's mpmc channels, which name a thread by a thread-local's address.

## 2026-11-19: Go's build cache kept warm: the gate's cap 40 GiB, relative to the free disk, never under a live build (n-gate-gocache)

- Measured: `test/gate/caches.edn`'s `{gocache}` row capped `/root/.cache/go-build` at 8 GiB by the least recently used (GD4), and
  the cheap prune runs at every gate's start and before a step every 5 minutes. This morning's prune removed 21 GiB, last night's
  28.7 GiB; the earlier nights' logs (`.tmp/gate*/`, `.tmp/night*/`) show removals of 1 to 16.9 GiB a pass. So the builds' warm
  set (`--gate-build`, javac's tool, the fixpoint's G2 and G3) is about 8 + 21 to 8 + 28.7, 29 to 37 GiB, and each gate's builds
  started nearly cold: go-build 79 min, javac-tool 71 min, the fixpoint 81 min, against about 8 min warm for `--gate-build`. Today
  at 09:57 UTC the cache held 10.5 GiB (4.3 GiB used within the hour, 6.2 GiB within 6 h), the disk 78% of 207 GB, 46 GB free.
- The rule (`bin/lib/gate-run.bash`'s `caches_rows`, `caches_prune`, `caches_go_busy`): a `[:size G :lru]` row takes
  `:free-gib F` (the cap min(G, its size + the free disk - F)), `:min-gib M` (never under M) and `:idle-only true` (nothing removed
  while a process whose executable is under `ARBACE_GOROOT` runs on the host: go, compile, link, asm; the user's rule, never trim
  the cache under a live build). The row: `[:size 40 :lru] :free-gib 35 :min-gib 8 :idle-only true`: 40 GiB holds the measured warm
  set, 35 is GD4's floor (`GATE_DISK_FLOOR`, 25 GiB) and 10, so the cache yields before the floor defers steps, and 8 is the old
  cap. GD4's floor and its deferral are unchanged; under a live build the floor's deferral waits for the build and the next cap.
- Dry run now (`bin/gate --prune --dry-run --cheap`): "/root/.cache/go-build holds 10.5 GiB, 44.8 GiB free: its cap 20.3 GiB",
  nothing removed (the old cap would have removed 2.5 GiB). On a disk with 70 GiB free the cap is 40 GiB.
- Alternatives: a fixed 40 GiB (fills the disk toward the floor on a full night); the LRU sparing the entries of the last N builds
  (Go's cache records no build, only entries' mtimes, refreshed at most hourly: a per-build index would be a tool of its own); a
  GOCACHE per run (cold every time, as night 13 found).
- Expected: the second and later builds of a night warm (go-build about 8 min in place of 79, javac's tool and the fixpoint alike
  when their packages fit), about 3 hours a night with the three builds, the disk at most 35 GiB from full by the cache's share.
- Tests: `test/gate/caches-test.bash` (17 ok: the free-relative cap, the minimum, a Go build running), `--coverage`,
  `test/docs/claude-md-test.bash` pass; CLAUDE.md's sentence on the 8 GiB cap updated. Keys: `gate_key` and the runtime's do not
  move (`bin/lib/gate-run.bash` and the table are in neither; the table is in no key); the steps `caches-table` (the table and
  its test), `claude-md` (CLAUDE.md) and `gate-tests` (`test/gate/`, `bin/lib/gate-run.bash`) rerun.

## 2026-11-19: Go's build cache by one rule by hand too: `bin/arbace-go --build`'s trim takes the gate's cap (n-gocache-trim, on `cd498e1d9`)

- Why: n-gate-gocache gave the gate's prune the cap min(40, size + free - 35) GiB, at least 8, idle-only, but every
  `bin/arbace-go --build` run by hand still removed every entry of Go's build cache unused for 90 minutes
  (`bin/lib/gocache.bash`'s `gocache_trim`): about 10:00 today it cut the cache from 10.5 to 6.4 GiB, the next build cold.
- Done: `bin/lib/gocache.bash` holds the rule once: `gocache_cap_kib SIZE FREE MAX [FREE_GIB [MIN]]` (the cap) and
  `caches_go_busy` (moved from `bin/lib/gate-run.bash`, which now sources gocache.bash and computes `caches_prune`'s cap by the
  same function). `gocache_trim` now does nothing while a Go build of `ARBACE_GOROOT` runs, nothing while the cache is under its
  cap (no age-based wipe while there is disk to spare), else removes the least recently used down to the cap; its numbers
  `ARBACE_GOCACHE_MAX_GIB` 40, `_FREE_GIB` 35, `_MIN_GIB` 8 repeat the table's `{gocache}` row (the build does not read
  `test/gate/caches.edn`, so go-build's audited inputs do not grow; the test holds them equal). `ARBACE_GOCACHE_KEEP_MIN` keeps
  its meaning as a bound: no entry used within that many minutes is removed (default 90; the gate's 7200), even over the cap.
  `ARBACE_GOCACHE_TRIM_DRY=1` lists without removing. `build_go_print_cache_trim` (repr/go's print cache in `.tmp`) unchanged.
- Tests: `test/gate/gocache-trim-test.bash` (new, a `gate-tests` member; 11 ok on a scratch cache: the defaults equal the
  table's, the cap's three cases, nothing under the cap though 11 of 12 entries are hours old, the 4 least recently used over it,
  KEEP_MIN's bound, a Go build running, the dry run), `test/gate/caches-test.bash` (17 ok) and `test/docs/claude-md-test.bash`
  pass; CLAUDE.md's sentence on the trim rewritten. Go's real cache was never trimmed.
- Keys: `bin/arbace-go` and `bin/lib/gocache.bash` are both in `gate_key` (and `gate_rest_key`: bin/lib less repr-java, repr-c,
  ci, gate-run.bash, cover.bash and the crops'), so this commit moves `gate_key` once: one rebuild of the gate's executables
  (two Go-hosted builds, about 8 minutes) and the checks on `:gate`/`:prog` rerun; `bin/lib/gate-run.bash` is in no key (the epoch).
- Alternatives: the build reading the table's row (an undeclared read of go-build's audit, or a new input for every build step);
  calling `caches_prune` from the build (sources the whole runner); keeping the 90-minute wipe only below the disk floor (two
  rules again).

  `*err*` naming the class (no unit names it alone): the compiled class would lose its default methods again, the very bug 399 fixes, so it
  is no longer silent. Its doc string says why the unit's `:vars` are not recomputed (the added methods name only the class's static
  `__var` fields, `arbace.lang.IFn` and the interfaces' supers). Considered: throwing; not taken, as gen-class-define's catch would turn it
  into the evaluated class's failure and a warning keeps the program built.

  `gc-record-aot-form!` over a redefined `arbace.classes.native/compiled`: the unit naming the class alone replaced, the others kept; a
  missing name and a unit naming the class beside another both `:no-match`, warned, nothing replaced; control: no recording, nil.
- test/j2g/unit/genclass/g/{Hello,Sub,GenSub}.ae: a default inherited through a subinterface, `(.hello g.Sub/super)`, translated by j2g to
  the declaring interface's function `J_g_Hello_J_Hello__O` (item 4, j2g's side).

## 2026-11-19: n-hasattr: synth-c23's pp-has-attribute settled from C23's table

The conflict (mac/n-llvm-indep 475cda469 wrote pp-has-attribute's :expect as a0-a8 0, "C23's table gives dates other than
202311L"; mac/n-c-expect 658ecf7b1 kept it and made the case an exception judged by gcc's run) settled from ISO/IEC 9899:2024
itself: the final standard's __has_c_attribute table (§6.10.2 in the published numbering, the table N3220 gives) answers 202311L
for every standard attribute: deprecated, fallthrough, maybe_unused, nodiscard, noreturn, _Noreturn, unsequenced and
reproducible. The 201904/201910/202003/202202/202207 dates are the C2x working drafts' (N3096 and before), which clang 23.1.5
still answers (it prints 201904 201910 202106 202003 202202 202202 0 0 here); gcc 15.2 answers 202311 for all eight. The
test's lines therefore print a0-a8 1 (each `== 202311L`, a7 the __nodiscard__ spelling, a8 _Noreturn), a9 1 (gnu::packed is
1), a10 and a11 1 (unknown names 0), in_if 1. Wrong: the .expect (n-llvm-indep's hand-worked value). Right: Arbace's target
(c/target/dialect.edn's :c23-attribute-version 202311, has.tsv's rows; no target change) and gcc's recorded run
(ref-gcc15.edn's stdout 26e290c4..., now byte for byte the .expect's digest). Done: table.edn's :expect all 1, `bin/ci synth`
(`--check` clean), the exception dropped from test/c/selfref-exceptions.edn (the case judged by its own .expect again);
`bin/ci check --corpus synth-c23 --only` on the file: pass 1. llvmi's c-O0/c-O2.synth.pp-has-attribute modules are clang's IR,
whose preprocessing answered the draft dates, so the .expect is not their outcome: arbace/llvm/check.ae's own verdict leaves
them to lli's record (they pass by it as before). Alternative not taken: a per-front-end expectation in the table. The crops'
scores are not re-recorded here (one C case moves from gcc's record to its own verdict, two llvm modules the other way).

## 2026-11-19: n-py-eval: goi's liveness across a fallthrough (pyexpat's every element with content)

Lib/test under pyi (n-py-rec's records run, 367 modules judged): test_minidom's 46 errors and 4 of multiprocessing spawn's
were "SystemError: pyi: Go panic: reflect: call of reflect.Value.Interface on zero Value". Reduced: `pyexpat.ParserCreate().
Parse(b"<a>x</a>", True)` fails with no handler set, on the gate's executable (01e4bb771) and on stage 0 (53da41d93) alike;
`debug.Stack()` in the interpreted pyexpat put it in expat's doContent (go/arbace/expat, xmlparse_doc.go), the switch on
m_parsingStatus.parsing whose `case XML_PARSING:` uses `next` inside an `if` and then falls through into `default:`, which
assigns `s = next`. goi's liveness plan (arbace/go/build.ae, plan-stmt) planned each switch clause alone, so `next` (a cell:
its address is taken) was cleared after the `if`, and the clause fallen into read a nil cell; `GOI_LIVENESS=0` passed. Fix: a
clause ending in fallthrough keeps alive the variables the bodies it falls into use (the chain while they fall through); they
die after the switch as before. Test: test/goi/run/go/t/fallthrough.ae (a cell and an S-slot value, a chain of two
fallthroughs), its output gc's (printed by repr/go, built by TamaGo's go): base panics, head passes; the 24 interpreter
programs of test/goi/run pass on the checkout's goi (ARBACE_PATH, RT.toolSource). pyexpat probe: chardata, buffered, default
and comment handlers all parse. arbace/go/build.ae is embedded: gate_key moves (the executables rebuild at the next gate).
Not taken: rewriting the fallthrough in expat's Go (hides the bug from every other interpreted package).

## 2026-11-19: n-py-eval: goi's stub families for pyi's bytes-like callbacks (write-ahead)

test_ctypes' 31 errors (test_byteswap 8, test_pickling 8, ...) and test_memoryview's 1 are "pyi: Go panic: goi: compiled
code called a method of an interpreted type whose signature has no stub left (go/arbace/gotable.edn, :stubs)", with no
"no stub left" warning: the method has no family at all. The compiled runtime asserts pyi's bytes-like and buffer callbacks
through unnamed interfaces (py/bytes.go's `interface{ BytesLike() []byte }`, binascii's `interface{ WritableBytes() ([]byte,
bool) }`, memoryview's `interface{ BufferValid() error }`), which the table's families (the listed packages' named

## 2026-11-19: n-py-eval: built-ins pickled by reference as CPython's (open, static methods, __new__, classmethod_descriptor)

test_pickle's rows in no class and some of :c-accelerators' (the C classes run on the pure Pickler) were "Can't pickle
<built-in function open>: it's not the same object as _io.open", "... maketrans>: it's not found as __main__.maketrans",
"... <built-in method __new__ of type object>: it's not the same object as __main__.__new__", and test_c_methods' "TypeError
not raised by dumps" for dict.__dict__['fromkeys']. Fixed in go/arbace/py, after CPython 3.14.10's methodobject.c and
descrobject.c:
- builtins.open is _io.open and io.open, one object (builtins_io.ae): _io's "open" is the registered builtin, which calls
  its interpreter's _pyio.open (a staticmethod, kept per interpreter as its _io is made) instead of importing io and
  calling io.open each time; pickle then finds _io.open the same object.
- a built-in type's static method (str.maketrans, bytes.maketrans: METH_STATIC, m_self the type) reduces to
  getattr(type, name) and reprs as "<built-in method maketrans of type object at 0x...>"; tp_new's wrapper
  (object.__new__, int.__new__) reduces to getattr(type, '__new__') (func.ae, meth_reduce).
- classmethod_descriptor has no __reduce__ (PyClassMethodDescr_Type has no tp_methods; queue 290 had given it one), so
  pickling the descriptor itself is refused as CPython refuses it (descr.ae).
Proof: the 9 methods (PyPicklerTests and InMemoryPickleTests' test_c_methods, test_complex_newobj_ex,
test_builtin_functions; PyPicklingErrorTests' three newobj_ex) on the checkout's runtime: 9 of 9 (0 of 9 before); a probe:
`builtins.open is io.open is _io.open`, open's text and binary files, open as a class attribute not bound, pickle round
trips of str.maketrans, object.__new__ and open are the objects. The C classes' twins (CPicklerTests ...) run the same
pure Pickler, so about 19 rows of the records run.

## 2026-11-19: n-py-eval: multiprocessing's "[Errno 10] No child process" rows classed in :fork

The records run's largest group in no class (74 in the 527 modules judged at 18:45) was ChildProcessError in the three
start methods' test_misc (TestSyncManagerTypes 17, TestWait 4, TestTimeouts 1, tearDownModule: 23 each) and
concurrent_futures' forkserver initializer tests and tearDownModule. Cause, reproduced (`bin/pyi run` of a unittest suite
of test_misc's TestStartMethod then TestWait.test_wait, the driver's reap_children after each test; test_wait passes
alone): 3.14's default start method on Linux is forkserver, TestStartMethod's tests reset the start method to the default,
the forkserver process dies at its own os.fork() (pyi has none), test.support.reap_children reaps it, and every later
Process start (forkserver.ensure_running's os.waitpid(pid, WNOHANG)) and util._cleanup_tests' forkserver._stop
(os.waitpid(pid, 0)) raise ECHILD. A consequence of the user's no-fork decision (2026-11-04), so `:fork` (design) names
these 74 by name, its :why saying why (divergences.edn and divergences-315.edn). Left in no class: test_process_pool's
three ProcessPoolSpawnProcessPoolExecutorTest test_force_shutdown_workers* (spawn context: not this cause, not probed).

## 2026-11-20: JCS50-1 (a), the own ct.sym (branch `jcs50-release`)

The user decided JCS50-1 (a): ct.sym made by Arbace, so that Java's independence never drops; jcs50-release waits for it. The
constraints: no javac tool rebuild for it if another way serves, a bounded run (about 8 GiB a process, chunks if need be, the heavy
lock above 4 GiB), made once and cached by its inputs, pinned, out of every gate step but a weekly and an oracle one.

Studied: jdk26u at baf63fbe42b8758448fee570a9d9bb914272d259, `make/modules/jdk.compiler/Gendata.gmk` (CreateSymbols' build-ctsym
and its arguments), `make/langtools/src/classes/build/tools/symbolgenerator/CreateSymbols.java` (run, not vendored: read by repr/java
at make time from the jdk26u checkout at the pin, nothing of it committed), `src/jdk.compiler/share/data/symbols/` (its input), the
build tree's `spec.gmk` (SOURCE_DATE 1787576400, JDK_SOURCE_TARGET_VERSION 26, VERSION_PRE internal, USE_EXTERNAL_LIBZ true) and
`support/symbols/included-modules`. Nothing copied into the tree: no doc/ARBACE.md or LICENSE.md entry (the made ct.sym is kept in a
cache, not committed; its digest is).

Done: CreateSymbols read on last night's javac tool (`javac-60886b4973e7356caf1b`, REPR_JAVA_STALE_OK=1) and interpreted there by
`test/javac-platform/ctsym-run.ae` (gensrc-run.ae, the own platform's way for interpreted build tools); the JN7 alternative (compiled
into javac's world's buildtools) rejected: a tool build each time, 4,400 more lines in every build, for a minute's run. First run:
ExceptionInInitializerError in java.lang.constant (ConstantDescs and PrimitiveClassDescImpl initialize each other; entered from
PrimitiveClassDescImpl the cycle leaves ConstantDescs' CD_int null): the runner initializes ConstantDescs first, as a JDK's boot has it
(a jrt follow-up noted in the survey). Second run, over the own platform's cache's modules: 21,054 entries, all but 58 equal to the
build's; the 58 are Q/*/module-info.sig with a ModuleTarget attribute, from the jmods' descriptors the cache's modules carry where the
build passes its exploded image. Third run, over an exploded view (the cache's modules with its descriptors/MODULE/exploded.class, the
own build's exploded descriptors): byte for byte the build's ct.sym, 642d31ba38e4b2222b1992206863983e87fdc529d99ee4fe2d6b77c7d31ba6f4.
One process, 50 to 106 s, 1.75 to 1.8 GiB peak in five runs: not chunked (well under 8 GiB; per-module chunks would change the output,
CreateSymbols strips annotations whose class no module holds and maps packages to modules across modules), no heavy lock (under 4 GiB).

Built: `test/javac-platform/ctsym.bash` (sourced by bin/javac-vendor: ct_sym_make, ct_sym_own, ct_sym, ct_sym_build_make), the verbs
`ct-sym-own [--check]`, `ct-sym-rebuild`, `ct-sym-oracle`, `ct-sym-build [--check]`; `jdk/javac/ct-sym-build.edn` (the build's arguments,
derived from the build tree, checked by the oracle tier); `jdk/javac/ct-sym.sha256` now `# kind: own` (the digest unchanged, the own

rewritten to the worktree), stage 0 of the main checkout (`ARBACE_HOST_EXE`). The baseline, `bin/repr-haskell lib-stg
--package base --ifaces own --judge test/haskell/lib-stg-own-base-results.edn` at next: 584 of 1,072 bindings equal to GHC's

worktree (whys.ae: each module's first differences; names.ae: the external names GHC's closure uses more or fewer than ours over
the differing bindings; classes.ae: each differing binding in one heuristic class; cmp: a binding's two renamed closures; run-only:
lib-stg --only with the package's judge and its negative control).

**Causes found** (base's 488 differing bindings and ghc-internal's 1,950, by first difference and by the names they use), and
what this branch did with each:
- a wanted dictionary solved by an instance (`$fFractionalRatio $fIntegralInteger`) was its term at each use; GHC binds it once
  after the binding's dictionary lambdas (the implication's evidence bindings): the binding's arity, `:r`/`:u`, `case`/`let`
  and order differences (Data.Fixed's methods, Data.Bifoldable's default methods);
- INLINE pragmas were not honoured: GHC's -O0 Simplifier (FinalPhase) inlines a saturated call of an INLINE function of the

## 2026-11-20: cpp-rt-own: the lowered runtime's pack units by Arbace's code generator, and libcpp's 14 units generated

What: on branch `cpp-rt-own-1120` (from next `939037429`, mac), the C++ code generator (arbace/cpp: sema, template, abi, codegen;
arbace/repr/cpp's parser and types, arbace/repr/c's lexer for C++'s ud-suffixes) gained what the 32 units of the lowered runtime
that bin/cppi's route auto took from the pack cpp-runtime-ir asked first, and then (the coordinator, the same day: CP413 (a),
CP414 (a), the user's) what GCC 15.2.0's libcpp, the token check's reference to be, asked. Method: each unit generated by
`arbace.cpp.codegen gen-batch` with runtime_ours' options (scratch scripts in the worktree's .tmp), its defined external names
against the pack's IR (runtime-judge's names level); libcpp's against clang 23.1.5's IR of each unit, made by hand into .tmp (the
oracle tier's tool, as the pack's were). Light: no gate, no whole corpus; one generator process at a time but for a few probes
(the host's javac tool build peaked at 41 GB and the coordinator froze two probes once).

The causes (doc/cpp/CPP-SURVEY.md, "As built: cpp-rt-own", the table): the parser's lookup after a qualified declarator-id (the
class's or namespace's enclosing namespaces, the definition's template headers first; a namespace member defined outside it; a class
defined by a qualified name replacing its incomplete declaration, inline namespaces too; namespace lookup scopes no class's); clang's
string ud-suffixes s and sv; mangling (a dependent template-id's member call, T::* in signatures, a redefined class's members in the
definition's namespace and its type by when the entity was made, as clang names at first emission); constant initialization (a
constexpr constructor with an empty body, and any constexpr object the evaluator makes, its body's assignments too; initializer
elements folded by the evaluator; the evaluator's bit operations); sema (inline namespaces for qualified class and function
definitions, a static data member's initializer in its class, destructor calls on const objects, an implicit this in unevaluated

## 2026-11-21: jrt's ReentrantReadWriteLock implements ReadWriteLock (next's build fixed)

The night's merge (n-merge-1120b, next 09114f806) regenerated jdk/ with java-split-1120's chunked driver. Among its 54 new forms
are sun.nio.ch's AsynchronousFileChannelImpl, AsynchronousServerSocketChannelImpl, AsynchronousSocketChannelImpl and Port, which
keep a `new ReentrantReadWriteLock()` in a field typed `ReadWriteLock`. jrt's ReentrantReadWriteLock is hand-written Go
(go/arbace/jrt/locks.ae), a leaf that never implemented the interface j2g translates from
jdk/forms/java/util/concurrent/locks/ReadWriteLock.ae: no earlier class assigned one to the interface. So next's gate build failed at
go build (amd64): "*ReentrantReadWriteLock does not implement ReadWriteLock (missing method Is_ReadWriteLock)", five sites
(the Python records' build, .tmp/worktrees/next/.tmp/gate-build.log). No gate ran on the merge, by the user's decision, so the merge's
light checks (plan, reap, scores, records) could not see it.

Fix: the interface's three methods on *ReentrantReadWriteLock, ReadLock__Lock and WriteLock__Lock returning its read and write
locks (jrt's Lock) and the marker Is_ReadWriteLock. Its ClassInfo's :Interfaces still list only Serializable (getInterfaces() omits
ReadWriteLock); the interface's class is j2g's, not jrt's, so naming it there would tie jrt's own tests to the translated closure.
Proof: the gate build at this commit's key (below, in the next entry or the Python records' entry).

The gate build at 4e7f94757 then compiled jrt and failed in arbace/lang: `undefined: jrt.StackTraceElement_Cast` (lang/j2g_dyn.ae).
The regenerated jdk/ brings java.lang.StackWalker$StackFrame into j2g's dyn interfaces; its slot for toStackTraceElement() casts the
result with `jrt/StackTraceElement_Cast`, and jrt's hand-written StackTraceElement had none. Every other jrt cast the generated
program names is defined (521 used, a static comparison of the printed program with jrt's functions: only this one missing). Fix:
StackTraceElement_Cast in go/arbace/jrt/throwable.ae, as AtomicInteger_Cast and kin are written. (j2g's dyn slots could instead fall
back to Go's assertion for a hand-written class without a cast, as code.ae's casts do; left as it is, one function in jrt.)
## 2026-11-20: java-split-1120: repr/java's jdk reads in chunk processes (the gate's behemoths, part 1: the mechanism)

The user: "identify the resource hogging bottleneck steps in the gate and split the behemoth jobs". repr/java's share of the
store of passes' peaks: `repr-java-nojavac.jdk` 53.4 GiB, `repr-java-front.jdk` 48.3, `repr-java-attr.jdk` 41.6 (61.4 on night
13, OOM-killed), `jrt-convert` 40.1 GiB in 2,119 s (its convert 1,758 s), `repr-java-roundtrip.jdk` 28.8 (the whole steps'
`repr-java-attr` 40.1 and `repr-java-front` 28.8 are passes of 2026-10-27, before GT5's parts). Goal: no step above about
16 GiB, the same checks, verdicts, records and outputs byte for byte.

- What grows: all five are one `read-jdk` of java.base's closure (3,421 files at `next` 939037429, 3,372 at 42494a700) in one
  process: `arbace.repr.java/jdk` packs the files into chunks of about 150 (whole packages; 23 chunks), converts
  REPR_JAVA_THREADS (4) at once, a javac context each over its chunk with every other chunk's sources visible
  (REPR_JAVA_PATCH_ALL), and holds every chunk's units, their forms, until one `finish` writes them all (`(mapv deref
  futures)`): every unit's forms (about 0.85 MB a file and front, "As built: the jdk parts' memory") plus four javacs, at GOGC
  200. Under GOMEMLIMIT 26 or 28 GiB the live heap near the limit made the collector thrash: jrt-convert's read took 1,660 s
  and its step 41,672 CPU seconds (`.tmp/gate-pass/jrt-convert/a3ca8d99...log`, `conv/repr-java-nojavac.edn` :peak-rss 32.0 GB).
- Split: `test/repr/java/chunks.ae` (`repr.java.chunks`), `ARBACE_PATH=ROOT/test bin/repr-java main -m repr.java.chunks
  read-jdk ...`, read-jdk's arguments and output: with REPR_JAVA_PROCS=N and more than one chunk, jdk's chunks (the same
  files, patch directories, javac options and patch path: what each javac sees is what it saw) each read by a process of its
  own, N at once, the tool again (`/proc/self/exe`, REPR_JAVA_CHUNK naming the chunk, GOMEMLIMIT REPR_JAVA_PROC_GOMEMLIMIT's);
  the chunk's process converts it as jdk's thread does, writes its units' forms (write-output a package at a time: a package
  is in one chunk alone) and a summary, data alone, checked to read back as itself (the split's facts, sorted sets, sorted
  again); the first process copies the chunks, runs the others and merges the summaries in the chunks' order into finish's
  reports and lines (the written files in write-output's group-by order: the same keys inserted in the same order; the
  unreadable list, the edn errors' frequencies, repr-java-report/-split/-attr/-nojavac.edn); a failed chunk's process fails
  its files, its log shown. Without REPR_JAVA_PROCS, or with one chunk, `arbace.repr.java/jdk` itself.
- DECISION (reader untouched): the driver lives outside the reader, in test/repr/java (as jrt-convert's own namespaces live in
  test/jrt), not in `arbace/repr/java.ae`. A first version put it into `jdk` and `finish` (`report!` over summaries, finish one
  summary) with `REPR_JAVA_TOOL` exported by bin/repr-java; it gave the same outputs, but java.ae and bin/repr-java are in
  `repr_java_reader_hash`, which the four provenance files record (`bin/provenance-check`, an essential step): the change
  would have needed `bin/jrt-convert update`, `bin/javac-vendor convert`, `--java-fixtures update` and `--forms update` in the
  same commit (GTS36 (b)), the first of them the behemoth itself and jdk/ stale at `next` for other reasons (overlay changes
  of 416 and queue 398 since 42494a700, no update yet). Outside the reader: the provenance files, the reader hash, the javac
  key and gate_key stay; the price is that the driver repeats `jdk`'s plan (files, chunks, patch path, javac options) and
  `finish`'s report; the slice proofs below compare them with the reader's own.
- Proofs on a slice (java/util/stream, function, concurrent of jdk26u's java.base: 181 files, 2 chunks; javac's tool
  `javac-60886b4973e7`, the original code in a worktree at 42494a700): `--check --front both --split --attr native` (forms,
  repr-java-report, -split, -attr equal byte for byte; the logs equal but the times), `--check --no-javac` (forms and report
  equal; repr-java-nojavac.edn but its times and :peak-rss), `--full --origins` (forms equal); a failing chunk's process
  (a tool that exits 3): 181 FAILED, the summary line "0 converted, 181 failed".

the known dictionary, its AbsBinds wrapper inlined at its dictionary arguments. Our Core has no type arguments: the workers keep
the class method's polymorphic types. Options: (a, recommended) typed inlining: at a beta-reduction whose binder's type has type
variables and whose argument's type is known (core's exprType), the one-way match's substitution applied to the types of the
template's binders as the Simplifier clones them (a clone forced where the substitution changes a type), and the AbsBinds
wrapper inlined at known dictionaries (its arguments' discount); about a day, the sizes: $fSemigroupIO and $fMonoidIO, ST's,
ReadP's and ReadPrec's instances, part of the update-flag class's 57 instance dictionaries (not measured which); (b) type arguments in

TypeRep (a :: k) gives (a :: k) ~ (Type :: Type), hence k ~ Type; our [:tc TypeRep [a]] has no invisible kind argument.

  (>>) in scope (GHC.Rename.Env's lookupSyntaxName: the unqualified name's lookupOccRn), and the elaborator types a bind statement as
  tcSyntaxOp does (the operator's type first, the continuation checked against its second argument, skolemised when that is a polytype:
  InfDo's `forall a. a -> InfDo`), its HasCallStack frame "a do statement" at the statement (T22086's expected stack). Only under
  RebindableSyntax; the standard path is byte for byte as before (its wanteds' order kept).

  superclass). derive-all! knew the class's kind only for the module's own classes; class-last-arity now reads an imported class's
  last parameter's kind from its methods' types (ctx-kinds' rule; else a superclass whose last argument is that parameter), and a
  request of arity 1 drops the type's last argument (GHC.Tc.Deriv's deriveTyData), anyclass and multi-parameter requests included.

  hole, a typeError of GHC.Tc.Errors' message at run time. The elaborator makes an unbound `_x` a hole (HsUnboundVar), its evidence a
  placeholder typeError filled once the binding group is solved (hole-text): Found hole with its type and the hint of a named hole,
  the contexts (the hole's own expression none: addExprCtxt skips HsUnboundVar), the relevant bindings (the group's binders, unfiltered
  for a hole) and the valid hole fits (GHC.Tc.Errors.Hole: the binders first, "bound at", then the imports' names, the renamer's GREs
  with their ImportSpec, "imported from ‘Prelude’ at FILE:1:1 (and originally defined in ‘M’)"; GHC.Internal.Err's left out,
  not_trivial; each candidate checked by tcCheckHoleFit's rule in a sandbox: instantiated, unified with the hole's type, every
  constraint solved by the instances or a defaulted call stack; sorted by the size of its type applications, at most 6). The text of all
  three is GHC's byte for byte (readLn @() and mempty @(IO ()) found among Prelude's 250 names). bin/lib/hsi/check passes
  -fdefer-typed-holes to the front end as it passed -fdefer-type-errors.

  MkSolo# of a fresh binder (Unarise's unariseAlts gives a DEFAULT alternative on a multi-valued scrutinee that tuple's), a right-hand
  side ok for speculation left a let. 19 of 19 cases as GHC's.

  constructor's unlifted field whose type the untyped Core leaves open (a representation-polymorphic result; a cast's result type,
  erased by simplify's strip) became a lazy thunk, read as an integer. tostg now case-binds such an argument with the field's

  not. type-reps now takes a newtype's representation type (newtype-rep: the constructor's result type matched against the

  one negative literal (LexicalNegation, NegativeLiterals) is negate applied to the positive literal, because an Integer's or

  :: TYPE ry -> Type)` is built with FUN's kind arguments 'Many, LiftedRep, LiftedRep (typeable-term's HF10-P39 (a) constants) where

## 2026-11-22: cpp-rt-own3: C++20's constraint mangling, constant POD locals, emission-order naming; 7 more runtime units own

Branch `cpp-rt-own3-1121` from mac/next 863bdaea1 (cpp-rt-own2 cd912b25f in it; the lowered runtime 187 of 198 units own, C++'s eval
and AOT 0.986 each). The brief (the main session, toward the CoMaIn goal): cpp-rt-own2's three decisions taken as recommended
(cpp-rt-own2-1 (a), -2 (a), -3 (a)), then floating_to_chars' VLAs and probes of valarray, floating_from_chars and tzdb if time
allowed, and the constinit union wrapper's lost vptr if on the way. Light and targeted, no gate; probes by `arbace.cpp.codegen
gen-batch` with runtime_ours' options, each unit's names against the pack cpp-runtime-ir's IR (n-all5's runtime build); each rule on
a reduced case against clang 23.1.5's IR recorded by hand with the host's clang++ (the oracle tier's tool), as cpp-rt-own2 did.

What was done (574e72fbf, the code; doc/cpp/CPP-SURVEY.md, "As built: cpp-rt-own3", the details):

1. DECISION cpp-rt-own2-2 (a), C++20's constraint mangling: a constraint scope that is not instantiated (template.ae's
   constraint-scope: the enclosing class specializations' template parameters at depth 0 up, the template's own at the next, the
   class templates' member typedefs over them), the texts a constraint writes as types resolved there at instantiation
   (constraint-q); Tk with arguments, trailing requires-clauses after the parameters (a templated member's too, sema's :tq), sizeof
   and alignof, T::x of a type parameter, template-id qualifier levels, nested dependent names flattened with each prefix a
   candidate. Units: c++20/sstream-inst.cc (string_view's iterator-pair constructor), c++23/print.cc (with span's range constructor,
   basic_string()'s trailing clause, ranges' _Size and _Data).
2. DECISION cpp-rt-own2-1 (a): codegen's const-local! (a POD local's constant initializer as clang's EmitAutoVarInit: memset, memcpy
   from `__const.FN.VAR`, or memset and few stores); the evaluator's unknown objects (an automatic or static object's lvalue formed
   without a read; since C++23 the object a reference variable outside the evaluation refers to, P2280R4) and an empty class's
   reference argument evaluated (basic_string::max_size()'s `_M_get_allocator() const` called and max_size inlined as clang). Unit:
   c++26/text_encoding.cc.
3. DECISION cpp-rt-own2-3 (a): names that differ by a redefined class's two paths written as placeholders with the earliest place
   (the unit's token order) they are referred from and resolved after the module (codegen's redef-name, redef-resolve!; abi's
   *redef-hook* under every public mangler): an explicit instantiation's members at the instantiation, a non-inline definition at
   its own token, constexpr specializations made before the definition named there, the class's own members in the definition's
   namespace. Units: c++17/fs_dir.cc, exp/filesystem/dir.cc, exp/filesystem/cow-dir.cc (cow-fs_dir.cc's names unchanged).
4. On the way: inline const variables external and linkonce_odr (print's customization point objects); a constructor template a

`typeRep @((->) x :: TYPE ry -> Type)`, which GHC solves as doTyApp's `(FUN 'Many @rx @ry) x`, doTyConApp giving mkTrCon $tcFUN
[SomeTypeRep 'Many, SomeTypeRep rx, SomeTypeRep ry] with rx's and ry's evidence from the givens (the IsTYPE matches' TypeRep
patterns). The solver gave the constants 'Many, LiftedRep, LiftedRep (HF10-P39 (a)'s unapplied arrow), so eqTypeRep failed and App
printed the TrApp unrebuilt. Now (typecheck.ae's arrow-tycon-ev, HF9-P4's erased kinds undone there alone): q is the first
argument's kind, TYPE q, its annotated kind (TrApp's (b :: k1)) rewritten by the given equalities in force (the IsTYPE match's
k1 ~ TYPE rx), else a kind link's (typeRepKind's, mkTrFun's); r the result kind's argument from the type's kind signature (hs-type's
HsKindSig kept beside the type, *kind-sigs*); each one's evidence a closed one's mkTrCon or the solver's (a given), LiftedRep where
no kind is known (GHC's defaulting). ghc-internal's STG: GHC.Internal.Data.Typeable.Internal alone moves (mkTrAppChecked's list now
[Many, $dTypeable rx, $dTypeable ry], GHC's shape); T14236 prints `Int# -> [Char]`.

  the helper's TSVs left as dumped. A separate script on purpose: pydump.py's digest keys every member of the python-pydump packs

  records'. With REPR_PYTHON_RT_LEVELS=recorded (the packs' rows, which keep positions) level 3 is implied by level 2 (compare
  --recorded): a compile without positions is a function of the ast without attributes.

  passed and the method held $dm's partial application (secretary: hsi's case on a PAP).

in chunks of at most 4096 bytes between polls (with the wake pipe, the handlers run on a signal).

## 2026-11-22: classes defined from class-file bytes (JD3): the loader, the interpreter and the verifier (java-bytecode-1122)

The user's decision JD3 of 2026-11-22 (the entry above): Java classes defined from class-file bytes built in full, a
class-file loader with a bytecode interpreter and verifier. Branch java-bytecode-1122 from mac/next 195fafabb; the
design note doc/classes/BYTECODE-SURVEY.md (the rows, where it goes, the loader, the interpreter, the verifier, the
stages, what it does not do; its "As built: stages 1-3").

Design taken: a class defined from bytes is an interpreted class of the Java forms' interpreter (a Compiler$CF$Klass made
through the host, Compiler$CFGo$GoHost on Go: Dyn objects, Dyn's slots, the member tables, CF$Klass.init's JLS 12.4.2,
the shadow stack of stack traces), its methods CF$Meths whose body (BytecodeBody, a CF$Node) runs their bytecode; the
loader, the interpreter and the verifier are Java forms in arbace/lang (Bytecode.ae, BytecodeFile.ae, BytecodeCode.ae,
BytecodeVerifier.ae), translated into the executable and into every program, so they mix with the Java forms' classes

## 2026-11-23: hsi collects the program's unreachable CAFs (unpack_sums_6's memory, the user's decision (b)) (smalls2-1123)

The user's decision of 2026-11-23 on testsuite/unboxedsums/unpack_sums_6 (out of memory at 16 GiB): (b) fix hsi so dead values stop
holding memory, then measure and cap. The cause found was a CAF, not a frame's dead locals: GHC -O0 floats the program's
`makeUnlayered magnitude` to the top level, and hsi's evaluated CAFs were Go roots for the whole run, so the 10-million-cell list
stayed. Built (go/arbace/hs/cafgc.ae new, rts.ae's marker `caf` mode, load.ae's and image.ae's `noteCAF`, machine.ae's
`schedDepth` and `cafCheck`; edited as Go by `bin/hsi runtime print`, read back by `bin/hsi runtime read`; fdwait.ae restored, its
committed hand comment the read does not keep; go/arbace/hs is a crop path, out of every key): past a 1 GiB Go heap (then twice
the last), hsi marks from its roots, a blackholed thunk's code not followed (GHC's blackhole has no SRT), and reverts the program's
own (unit main) evaluated CAFs the mark did not reach, as GHCi's revertCAFs; the libraries' CAFs never. Alternatives not taken:
reverting every CAF (stdout's handle and the RTS's named closures would be at risk of a second evaluation); a CAF list never
collected but cleared after main's first reference (not GHC's rule). Proof: unpack_sums_6 on the own libraries at a 6 GiB cap
completes (104.8 s of CPU, 2.4 GB peak); its negative control, the same build with HSI_CAF_GC=0, runs out of memory at 5 GB. Its
own verdict is a timing comparison that -O0 leaves to chance (all.T marks the test fragile(22504)): exit 0 on the first run, 1 on
the capped record run (not recorded); further runs measure the rate for the coordinator. doc/haskell/HASKELL-EVAL-SURVEY.md, "As
built: the program's CAFs collected".

in front of two flock slots, `big.lock` (slot 1, still the plain flock agents take with `flock big.lock CMD`) and
`big.lock.2`; a state file beside each new ticket (`.s-TIME-PID`: wait, 1 or 2, and the need) tells holders from waiters, so
the head is the first waiter, and holders no longer block the queue. A second job runs only when MemAvailable less 2 GiB, less
the other holders' declared needs not yet reached (need less process tree RSS), exceeds its `HEAVY_MEM_GIB` (default 24;
`all`: never beside another); the head that does not fit waits and nothing passes it. The gate passes each step's admission
as its `HEAVY_MEM_GIB`, and `--concurrent`'s whole-run hold `all`. doc/GATE-SURVEY.md, "As built: the big lock's two slots";
CLAUDE.md's sentence; the Makefile's `gate-queue` line; `test/gate/heavy-lock-test.bash`.

Interop with the one-slot waiters queued during the change (six at the time): their tickets carry no state file and are read as
the old protocol's (they wait for every earlier ticket, then for slot 1), so a new waiter after one takes slot 2 only, under
the memory rule, and never slot 1 before it. Deployed into the main checkout by writing the file beside it and renaming it
over, so the running bash instances keep reading the old inode.

Alternatives weighed: a counted semaphore in one file (rejected: plain `flock big.lock` users would no longer be excluded);
renaming tickets to mark holders (rejected: the old waiters compare names and contents); the memory rule on MemAvailable alone,
as stated (taken with the holders' unreached declarations subtracted: a gate build just started shows almost nothing in
MemAvailable and reaches ~22 GiB minutes later, so MemAvailable alone would admit a second build into an OOM); probing slot 1
through /proc/locks (taken only for `--queue`'s display; admission probes with `flock -n`, which is atomic).

## 2026-11-23: cpp-ce2, the checker's constant evaluator (branch `cpp-ce2-1123` from mac/next `69bb781b5`)

The burst's C++ read stream "cpp-ce2" (the coordinator's brief: the constant evaluator's gaps, the largest cause group of the read
cell's deferred rows; cpp-rt owns c++20/tzdb.cc and the runtime build). All in arbace/cpp/sema.ae's checker mode (`checking?`), with
two parser and two diag additions; the code generator's folds unchanged but for one lookup. The rules from the standard's text
([expr.const], [basic.life], [bit.cast], [expr.dynamic.cast], [expr.new], [expr.delete], [class.dtor], [class.temporary],
[class.union.general], [dcl.init.aggr], [temp.point]) and GCC 15.2's behaviour as the tests record it; no GCC or clang code read.

- Unions: arbace/repr/cpp/parse.ae `designate` keeps a union's one designated element's member as the InitListExpr's `field`
  (clang's semantic form); Sema's "InitListExpr" carries it as :field and the aggregate branch initializes that member; an empty
  list takes a default member initializer's member ([dcl.init.aggr]/5). cpp2a/constexpr-union7.C's `g({.f = 3.14})` now reaches C++17's
  "change of the active member".
- Pointers to data members evaluated ({::mdata [class path]}, `.*`/`->*`'s :mfield): cpp2a/constexpr-98122.C.
- __builtin_bit_cast: the native parser's BuiltinExpr keeps the type-id and operand (:_bitcast, :_bctype; the converter writes its text
  as before); Sema's `bit-cast-expr` (GCC's static errors: incomplete types, a variable's at its declaration, not trivially copyable,
  array destination, sizes) and the evaluator's `ce-bit-cast` (the type rules of [bit.cast]/3; the object representation as bits,
  padding, unnamed bit-fields and uninitialized members indeterminate; [bit.cast]/2's indeterminate result for unsigned char and
  std::byte, else GCC's "accessing uninitialized byte at offset N"). The code generator's mode refuses it as before.
- Lifetimes and destructors: explicit destructor and pseudo-destructor calls end lifetimes; reads, writes and destruction of an ended
  object are GCC's "outside its lifetime"; from C++20 a block's, a full-expression's temporaries' and a call's by-value parameters'

## 2026-11-23: cpp-ce3, the checker's constant evaluator: placement new, objects under construction, exact arithmetic (branch `cpp-ce3-1123` from mac/next `097078f5b`)

The burst's C++ read stream on the constant evaluator (arbace/cpp/sema.ae) after cpp-ce2; doc/cpp/CPP-SURVEY.md, "As built: cpp-ce3".
Each rule from the standard's text and GCC 15.2's behaviour as gxx-dg's tests record it; no GCC or clang code read.

Decision (the user, 2026-11-23): placement new in a constant evaluation is restricted to std::construct_at before C++26, as the
standard ([expr.const]/5.20.1 of C++20 and C++23) and GCC (is_std_construct_at) do; from C++26 allowed (P2747R2). Built: the evaluator
knows its calling function (a call's and a constructor's environment carry ::fn; `ce-std-construct-at?`), and the reserved placement
form outside std::construct_at is GCC's "call to non-'constexpr' function 'void* operator new(std::size_t, void*)'". This replaces
cpp-ce2's acceptance of every placement new from C++20. Alternative weighed: accepting it until a test needs the refusal (cpp-ce2's
choice; rejected by the decision: an acceptance GCC refuses is a wrong answer too).

Built (the checker's, `checking?`): the dynamic type of an object under construction ([class.cdtor]/6: `*ce-bases*`, the cells of
objects whose constructors are building their bases; a dynamic_cast's operand in a constructed base subobject takes that base as its
most derived object, one in a base not constructed yet GCC's "accessing uninitialized member"); a default member initializer's errors
at the use (`ce-dmi-at`, the item's :dmi-range); exact 64-bit arithmetic (unsigned modulo 2^64, signed past its range the sure "value
N is outside the range of representable values"; shared with the code generator's folds, which had thrown Java's ArithmeticException)
and, found on the way, the signed range check's bounds exact: (bit-shift-left 1 63) is a long's Long/MIN_VALUE, so every 64-bit signed
+, - and * (`5LL + 3LL`) had been "outside the range" in the checker; GCC's -fconstexpr-loop-limit (`ce-loop-limit!`, the step budget
3,000,000 in the checker so that the limit comes first); "used before its definition" (`ce-undefined?`, `*ce-point*` the evaluated
declaration's range, `*ce-mi-at*` a mem-initializer's range: the native parser's CXXCtorInitializer keeps it as the private :_range,
no tree check reads underscore keys); immediate invocations evaluated (`cx-immediate-eval!`, not in an immediate function context, a
conditional's branch, a default argument or a default member initializer); delete through a base pointer and a member call on freed
storage; GNU statement expressions evaluated; the potential constant check's do body.
